baseline.tasksSurfaceBefore: one registration route on the Tasks port (crates/suite-runtime/src/auxiliary.rs) that validates and discards the queue config; enqueue, delete and /queueStats answer 501 UNIMPLEMENTED; nothing ever registers a queue

precedence: firebase-tools-15.22.0-tasks-emulator (with its Functions emulator and the Admin SDK task-queue client)
oracles.classificationRule: the official emulator wins; a divergence is allowed only for a documented emulator defect (a corrupting or nondeterministic path) where a safe behaviour is followed instead, named in the fixture README and asserted in the replay

dispatch: token bucket per queue (maxDispatchesPerSecond, one-second refill, empty at start)
retry ladder with maxAttempts, maxRetrySeconds, maxBackoffSeconds, maxDoublings, minBackoffSeconds
execution count incremented on non-5xx failures only
notInScope: scheduleTime as a delay (the official emulator ignores it)
OIDC / Authorization on dispatch (the SDK skips verification under the emulator)
queue pause/resume/purge, task list/get, the Cloud Tasks v2 API surface
persistence or export (the official emulator has none)
an Emulator UI tab (the official UI has none)

normalizedFields: attempt counter of the dispatch-deadline program (per worker)

emulatorReplay.test: conformance/src/functions-runtime/replay-fireside.ts --profiles tasks --fixture fixtures/tasks-v1/emulator-programs.json (npm run replay:functions:runtime); the same runner and normalization as the capture, against the Fireside suite serving the same synthetic project
emulatorReplay.timingSteps: retry, deadline and rate programs replay against the real clock; the corpus records counts and header values, not durations

unit.coverage: every route status/body from the corpus, the dispatch header set, the retry ladder, the deadline abort, the concurrency and rate limits, discovery from an inventory

queueRegistry.policy: queues are registered in-process from the Functions inventory at readiness and after every reload (replacing the config, never deleting a queue), and the registration route stays available for callers; the official emulator's queue id is the bare function name and its location the region

dequeuedTaskDeletion.policy: deleting a task that already left the pending queue answers 200 and decrements the count exactly as the official emulator does (the corpus pins numberOfTasks: -1), but Fireside never re-dispatches or corrupts its queue as the official linked list does when other tasks are pending

persistence.policy: in-memory like the official emulator; no export

k1.oracle: firebase-tools 15.22.0 emulators:start --only auth,functions,firestore,storage,pubsub,eventarc,tasks,extensions on the Phase H synthetic project with the tasks primary codebase; firebase-functions 7.2.5, firebase-admin 13.10.0, Java 25 for the Firestore emulator
